mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes GLC 350d or 400d engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rebuilt GLC 350d OM642 engine costs £3,500-£5,500 supply-only; a rebuilt GLC 400d OM656 engine costs £4,500-£7,500 supply-only. Fitting adds £800-£1,500 depending on complexity - the OM656's inline-six is slightly more accessible than the OM642's V6.

mainEntity.name: Is the Mercedes GLC 350d V6 diesel reliable? What are the common problems?

acceptedAnswer.text: The OM642 V6 is fundamentally robust but has one dominant weak point - oil cooler seals that leak into the engine V. Catch it early and the engine will exceed 200,000 miles. Ignore it and oil starvation destroys the bottom end.

mainEntity.name: Is the Mercedes GLC 400d straight-six reliable? What should I watch for?

acceptedAnswer.text: The OM656 straight-six is a modern, powerful diesel with excellent performance - 330hp and 700Nm. However, a global recall for coolant pump vacuum leaks affected approximately 800,000 OM654/OM656 vehicles. Ensure your GLC 400d has had the recall performed.

mainEntity.name: How long do Mercedes GLC 350d and 400d engines last?

acceptedAnswer.text: Properly maintained OM642 V6 diesels routinely reach 200,000-250,000 miles before major work. The OM656 straight-six is too new for definitive long-term data, but early indications suggest similar longevity with proper maintenance.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in my Mercedes GLC 350d or 400d?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if the GLC is otherwise in good condition with no rust or major electrical faults. A rebuilt OM642 costs £3,500-£5,500 - far less than replacing a £15,000-£40,000 vehicle. The GLC 400d's higher value (£25,000-£40,000) makes replacement even more financially justifiable.

mainEntity.name: What oil does my Mercedes GLC 350d or 400d need?

acceptedAnswer.text: Mercedes-Benz specifies low-SAPS oil meeting MB 229.51 or 229.52 - typically 5W-30. The OM642 V6 requires approximately 8.5 litres; the OM656 straight-six requires approximately 8 litres.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes Benz GLC Class 350d/400d - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The GLC 350d launched in 2016 as the torquey six-cylinder diesel flagship of the X253 GLC range, offering V6 refinement and 258hp. In 2019, the GLC 400d replaced it with a new-generation 2.9L straight-six OM656 - more powerful, more efficient, and with a radically different engine architecture.

milestones.description: X254 second-generation launched; 400d designation discontinued (OM656 retired from GLC range)

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Mercedes Benz GLC Class 350d and 400d is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points - from the V6 oil cooler seals to the straight-six coolant pump recall.

items.title: 3.0L V6 Diesel (2016-2019)
items.commonFailure: Oil cooler seal degradation - the seals between the engine block and oil cooler (located in the engine "V" between cylinder banks) leak over time, allowing oil to pool in the V and eventually drip onto the exhaust, causing burning smells and, if ignored, low oil pressure and bottom-end failure. Typical failure mileage: 70,000-110,000 miles.

items.title: 2.9L Straight-Six Diesel (2019-2022)
items.commonFailure: Coolant pump vacuum leak recall - a leak can develop between the coolant pump and the vacuum circuit, allowing coolant to enter the vacuum system, affecting components and potentially leading to increased temperature and fire risk. Mercedes issued a global recall for OM654 and OM656 diesel engines (2017-2021) addressing this fault. Water pump failures and post-recall instability have also been reported.

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes Benz GLC Class 350d/400d Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The GLC 350d's OM642 V6 and the GLC 400d's OM656 straight-six are both fundamentally robust diesel engines, but each has a well-documented Achilles' heel that drives replacement decisions. The OM642's oil cooler seals leak deep in the engine V - a £5 part that costs £900 in labour to replace. The OM656's coolant pump vacuum leak triggered a global recall, and post-repair complications have left some owners facing difficult decisions. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components addressing the original failure point, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: OM642 Oil Cooler Seal Failure - The V6 Diesel's Expensive Leak
problems.rootCause: The oil cooler seals (A6421880480) located in the engine V between cylinder banks degrade over time. Oil leaks into the V and drips onto the exhaust, producing a burning smell. If ignored, oil starvation destroys the bottom end. The seals themselves cost approximately £5-£10; the labour is 9-12 hours.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove intake manifold, fuel injectors, wiring harness to access and replace seals (oil cooler and turbo oil feed). 9-12 hour job.
repairOptions.longevity: 60k-80k miles - original seals will eventually fail again

repairOptions.tier: Full Replacement - Rebuilt OM642 engine with upgraded seals
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt OM642 engine with upgraded Viton oil cooler seals, new injector seals, turbo oil feed pipe, full gasket set
repairOptions.longevity: 100k+ miles - upgraded seals resolve the design flaw

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2016-2019 GLC 350d 4MATIC is worth approximately £15,000-£25,000 depending on mileage and condition. The GLC 350d sits in the £15,000+ band - replacement cost is typically small relative to vehicle value, making a full rebuilt engine a justifiable investment for owners planning to keep the car.
problems.recommendation: If you catch the leak early (small puddle on the undertray, occasional burning smell but no oil pressure drop), the seal replacement alone is the right move - but use a specialist who fits upgraded Viton seals, not OEM. Many OM642 engines are written off because owners ignore the leak until oil starvation destroys the bottom end. On a GLC 350d worth £15,000-£25,000, £1,200 well spent at a specialist prevents a £5,000+ replacement.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt OM642 Mercedes GLC 350d engine prices

problems.h4: OM656 Coolant Pump Vacuum Leak - The Straight-Six Recall Crisis
problems.rootCause: A leak can develop between the coolant pump and the vacuum circuit, allowing coolant to enter the vacuum system. This affects components and can lead to increased temperature, potentially causing a fire. Mercedes issued a global recall for approximately 800,000 vehicles equipped with OM654 and OM656 diesel engines. The recall involves replacing the coolant pump switch valve and updating software - but parts shortages have delayed implementation.

repairOptions.tier: Recall Remedy - Coolant pump switch valve + software
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace coolant pump switch valve, update ECU software, vacuum system inspection
repairOptions.longevity: Manufacturer-mandated fix - ensure recall has been performed

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace coolant pump, vacuum lines, flush cooling system
repairOptions.longevity: If recall not performed or water pump has failed

repairOptions.tier: Full Replacement - Rebuilt OM656 engine with updated components
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt OM656 engine with updated coolant pump, new vacuum lines, full gasket set
repairOptions.longevity: If engine has suffered overheating damage from coolant loss

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2019-2022 GLC 400d 4MATIC is worth approximately £25,000-£40,000 depending on mileage and condition. The GLC 400d sits firmly in the £15,000+ band - replacement cost is modest relative to vehicle value. However, the recall nature of the primary fault means many owners will have the repair done at no cost.
problems.recommendation: Check if your GLC 400d has had the OM656 coolant pump recall performed - if not, contact your nearest Mercedes dealer immediately. The recall is free and addresses a genuine fire risk. If the recall has been performed and you're still experiencing cooling system issues, have a specialist inspect the water pump and vacuum lines. If overheating has caused cylinder head damage, a full rebuilt engine is the only safe option - the OM656 is too complex for most independent workshops to rebuild reliably.
